summary.headline: Sirca Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin reached 20.08%, with management guiding 25-30% growth and 19-21% EBITDA margin for FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 33.07% YoY to INR134.29 crore, EBITDA rose 35.69% to INR25.74 crore (margin 19.17% vs 18.8%), and PAT rose 25.07% to INR17.71 crore. For FY26, revenue was INR492.48 crore (+31.79%), EBITDA INR98.88 crore (+46.62%) and PAT INR65.05 crore (+32.48%). Management flagged short-term raw material margin pressure from crude-linked inputs, offset by two price increases totalling about 10% on Sirca range, and a March NC raw material shortage that cost Wembley about INR4-5 crore of revenue. The company has shifted from pure trading to manufacturing, with about 95% of previously imported products now targeted for Indian production.

segments.name: Core Sirca wood coatings
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of about INR372 crore, of which about INR124 crore came from Italy-imported products and about INR252 crore from products made in India. Sirca gross margins are higher than Wembley/Welcome by about 10-15 percentage points.

segments.name: Wembley and Welcome (acquired brands, mass segment)
segments.commentary: Combined FY26 revenue of about INR120.5 crore: Welcome about INR46.5 crore and Wembley about INR74 crore. Wembley was roughly flat YoY after INR4-5 crore of orders were lost in March to an NC raw material shortage, and about INR5-6 crore was billed to distributors before the acquisition closed.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY25 exports were about INR9 crore, mainly Nepal plus one or two Sri Lanka customers. Wembley Valentino polyurethane exports are expected to start in Q1 FY27, with management targeting exports of about 3-4% of revenue.

segments.name: Acrylic coatings (Sirca brand)
segments.commentary: Acrylic sales contributed about INR120 crore in FY26 per management. Made-in-India production is expected to roll out in Q1 FY27 after the December 2025 know-how transfer from Sirca Italy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% CAGR, described as a minimum.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in the 19-21% range, with raw material pressure expected to be temporary after two price increases.
Management said the INR1,000 crore revenue vision is achievable in about three years (FY29) and that Sirca and Wembley capacities are broadly sufficient for that journey.
FY27 capex limited to about INR5-6 crore, mainly for acrylic production expansion.
Expects inventory to fall by about INR15-20 crore and debtors to decline in the coming quarters as import stock is consumed by June end.
Expects NC supply constraints from supplier Nitrex to ease from June with a new Nitrex unit starting operations.
Expects exports to Middle East including Dubai to begin in FY27, and export contribution of about 3-4% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Sirca core facility capacity raised by 1,750 tons per annum to about 17,750 tons; about 12,000 tons utilised in FY26, with full utilisation expected by year-end in single shift at Unit 1.

Wembley capacity consolidated from four old distributor units into one new integrated facility with about 3x earlier capacity; management expects a turnover of INR250-300 crore from this setup using nitrocellulose and polyurethane products.
Wembley manufacturing facility is fully operational, consolidating multiple production lines.
Formula transfers for acrylic and polyester systems are complete; commercial trials underway with production expected in Q1 FY27. UV technology transfer is on track for Q1.
FY27 capex of about INR5-6 crore planned for acrylic production; most FY26 capex went to consolidating Wembley and Welcome sites.
demand_pricing: Two price increases of about 5% each (April and May 2026) on the Sirca range, totalling about 10%; Wembley and Welcome prices raised by about INR35 per litre. Management said this is enough to offset RM inflation so far.
Polyurethane is replacing melamine; melamine is about INR230-240 per litre vs PU about INR450-460 per litre, with PU about 10% higher per square foot on coverage.

Premium segment competition from large players is seen as limited because specification is driven by architects and designers; mass segment competition is more intense and is addressed through retailer margins and exclusivity.
About 80% of revenue comes from North India (Delhi NCR, Punjab, Haryana, UP, UK, Rajasthan, MP) and about 20% from West and South; 5 of 20 depots opened last year in South and West.
Management said the Indian furniture industry is shifting to local manufacturing after BIS implementation, which supports OEM and institutional demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between Sirca Italy-imported, Sirca India-made, Wembley and Welcome?
qa_highlights.answer: Core Sirca about INR372 crore (about INR124 crore imported from Italy, about INR252 crore made in India); Welcome about INR46.5 crore and Wembley about INR74 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook given crude-linked raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term pressure for about 10-15 days before price increases took effect; gross margins expected to be maintained after two price hikes; in-house production of previously imported products to add margin benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue growth and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 25-30% CAGR, EBITDA margin in the 19-21% range; INR1,000 crore revenue target achievable in about three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Wembley growth story and why was it flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat YoY due to about INR5-6 crore pre-acquisition billing and a March NC shortage costing about INR4-5 crore; management expects real growth from FY27 as the transition period completes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material mix and price exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Resins and solvents make up about 95% of RM (solvents such as toluene, butyl acetate, PMA), with additives about 5% from BYK, Dow and Bayer; solvents and resins are sourced largely from dealers and reputed suppliers, with some resins made in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Why is working capital about twice that of Asian Paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition-related inventory build for the transition, slower Wembley/Welcome receivables tied to old owner payments, and about six months of imported acrylic inventory; about INR15-20 crore inventory reduction expected and receivables to ease.

qa_highlights.question: What is the parent company royalty and brand agreement term?
qa_highlights.answer: Parent receives 0.75% of total reported revenue, including Wembley; brand agreement with Sirca Italy runs till 2041.

risks_watch: Crude-linked raw material volatility from the Middle East conflict could keep gross margins under pressure until price hikes fully pass through.
NC cotton supply constraints from supplier Nitrex (diversion to defence) affect Wembley's nitrocellulose range until the new Nitrex unit is commissioned, expected from June.
Export logistics and vessel availability for flammable material are difficult; the 3-4% export contribution target depends on normalisation.
Working capital intensity is high; the company expects inventory and debtor reduction but has not quantified receivable days.
Wembley and Welcome gross margins are about 10-15 percentage points below Sirca; management expects EBITDA to be broadly unchanged, so mix shift is a margin watch point.
Competitive pressure in the mass segment from large paint companies.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the 25-30% growth and 19-21% margin guidance, but cautious on near-term margins and Wembley, which management attributed to raw material and transition issues. Answers on Wembley's flat growth and margin mix were direct, while export timelines were framed as conditional on the geopolitical situation.

we expect a minimum, considering the market situation and being, you know, being a little on the restricted side, we still see that 25% to 30% CAGR growth is what we expect as minimum.

adds.what: Sirca core facility capacity +1,750 tons per annum to about 17,750 tons
Wembley consolidated into one new integrated facility with about 3x earlier capacity (turnover INR250-300 crore medium term)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 25-30% (described as a minimum) and a 19-21% EBITDA margin, backed by a 1,750 t/yr Sirca capacity addition, Wembley consolidation (about 3x capacity), two ~5% price hikes, and Italy-to-India production shifts, though no firm order book was quoted.
